thread:
jenna (AcmeOps): Hey team — over the last hour we started getting 429s from the API. Our client telemetry says ~1,200 rpm and 18 tpm, but half the requests return 429s. Any ideas?

aaron: sorry to hear that — we'll help. Can you paste a sample request id from one of the 429 responses? Also which region / model?

jenna (AcmeOps): model=gpt-4-rt, region=us-west-2. sample x-request-id: rq_8f3a2c1b. client shows 1200 rpm at minute granularity.

mira: quick hypothesis: telemetry mismatch between client-side aggregate and per-route/host leaky-bucket enforcement. Do you use HTTP/2 multiplexing or many concurrent streams?

jenna (AcmeOps): yes we multiplex with up to 64 concurrent streams per connection using our SDK.

aaron: that could cause short bursts that exceed the per-minute window the rate-limiter enforces. Our service applies both RPM (requests/minute) and TPM (tokens/minute) plus per-route limits. The headers you should look for on responses: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset. Did you see any of those on 429s?

jenna (AcmeOps): only a couple of 429s had X-RateLimit-Remaining, most responses are just 429 with retry-after. sample response: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 1
X-Request-Id: rq_8f3a2c1b
```

mira: can you run a quick check on client-side pacing? e.g. log per-second request counts for 60s window. Multiplexing + many inflight streams often concentrates requests into tiny sub-minute windows.

jenna (AcmeOps): running now, attaching small output: we see bursts of ~400 req/sec for 3s every minute when many jobs flush concurrently.

aaron: that pattern will definitely trigger our burst protections even if avg rpm looks fine. Two paths: reduce client-side concurrency / add jitter, or request a per-tenant quota bump while we investigate.

sam_oncall: I'll pull server-side traffic for that request id. @rate-limiter-bot can you attach the rate-limiter trace for rq_8f3a2c1b?

rate-limiter-bot: attached trace-id rl_trace_2024_1723459999 (summary): request exceeded per-route burst bucket; token bucket drained at T+1s; local fallback to short-window reject. See logs: /var/log/rl/2024/1723459999/rq_8f3a2c1b.log

sam_oncall: confirms bucket exhausted. There are also concurrent requests from same tenant hitting multiple routes which counts against different internal sub-quotas.

mira: next steps for customer: 1) apply client-level smoothing: cap concurrency to ~8 streams, add randomized jitter 0-200ms before flush; 2) instrument per-second telemetry (not just per-minute) and share a 2-min sample; 3) send 5 failing x-request-ids (we have one).

aaron: I'll open a temporary throttle uplift request for AcmeOps while they deploy smoothing. Please note uplifts are short-lived and monitored.

jenna (AcmeOps): thanks — deploying smoothing now. small question: any suggested retry/backoff config? We currently retry immediately up to 3 times.

mira: please use exponential backoff with jitter: base=200ms, factor=2, max=5s, jitter=random(0, 200ms). Also prefer to respect Retry-After header when present.

jenna (AcmeOps): deploying backoff and reduced concurrency. Will replay after changes and post telemetry.

sam_oncall: for our engineering follow-up: can we add a short doc snippet about how HTTP/2 multiplexing + high concurrency can amplify bursts and how to calculate effective per-client burst? Could be a quick note in the SDK docs.

aaron: good idea — I'll add a runbook item: "If client uses HTTP/2 multiplexing, measure peak concurrent request flush and prefer client-side windowing (tokens) over blind parallelism."

mira: additional diagnostic shell commands for Jenna if useful: 
```
# grep logs for request ids
zgrep "rq_8f3a2c1b" /srv/logs/api/* | sed -n '1,200p'

# basic per-second RPS from local client logs (example)
awk '{print int($1)}' client.log | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -n 50
```

jenna (AcmeOps): thanks — sending 4 more x-request-ids and a 90s perf capture in 5m. Appreciate the fast response. :pray:

aaron: got them. we've provisionally approved a +2x short uplift for 30 minutes while you finish the deployment. Monitoring in place. If smoothing doesn't reduce 429s after that window, we'll scope a longer-term capacity change or deeper routing policy edits.

sam_oncall: logging follow-up action: create internal ticket RL-2024-189 to add SDK guidance + per-route telemetry headers in docs.

mira: marking thread resolved-for-now — reopen if 429s persist after smoothing. :thumbsup:
